Attempt count: 1/3 — the documented TR-NNN path form (path_params.test_run_id='TR-9062') worked immediately, no retries needed. project_id 379335744 + test_run_id 'TR-9062' + p=1/per_page=30 returned 200, info={page:1,page_size:30,count:5,prev:null,next:null}, 5 rows, top-level skipped_test_case_ids:[] present as documented, no data envelope (flat {success,info,test_cases}) — matches the declared contract's envelope shape exactly.

SCHEMA DRIFT: the describeCapability 200 JSON-schema's expanded item properties (assignee, creator_details, created_at, updator_details, updated_at, case_type, priority, status, case_type_imported, description, custom_fields, estimate, expected_result, id, identifier, is_automation, links, name, history_count, owner, preconditions, owner_imported, priority_imported, project_id, status_imported, steps, tags, template, test_case_folder_id, test_case_steps, lcnc_build_map, automation_status, issues, comments_count, metadata) are a strict SUBSET of what the row actually returns. Every declared field was present and correctly typed (declared_missing: none), but the actual row carries ~26 additional fields the expanded schema never lists. Critically, the fields the capability's own prose and top-level 'returns' summary treat as central to this endpoint's whole purpose — mapping_id, latest_status, test_case_id, test_run_id, configuration, test_assignee, last_executed_by, last_executed_at, planned_execution_date, execution_eligible, result_status, result_custom_fields, defects — are ALL present in the 'returns' name list and in guidance text ('mapping_id is the id every bulk operation on this run takes...') but are completely absent from the expanded JSON schema's properties block. So the schema-authoring is internally inconsistent: the free-text contract (returns[], guidance[]) correctly describes the row: the machine-checkable schema does not. An agent that validated strictly against the expanded schema would not even know mapping_id — the field the guidance calls indispensable for bulk ops — exists. The remaining ~13 undeclared fields (automation_state, is_shared, project_name, template_step_type, template_id, step_count, test_case_folders_path, test_run_results_count, test_run_results_issues_count, dataset_values, deleted, assignee_imported, result_notes) aren't named anywhere in the contract at all — pure surplus.

THREE-WAY COMPARISON — what actually separates the three run-case-listers:
1. get_test_run_cases_v1 (already inspected, not by me): despite its name/path suggesting a case list, its declared 200 shape is a run HEADER under a data envelope (data.test_run: progress counts, assignee, dynamic_filter, linked issues) — no per-case rows at all. It is not a case-lister; it's a run-summary endpoint that happens to sit in the same naming family. That's worth stating plainly rather than folding into 'differs from siblings': callers using this name to try to list cases will get zero case rows, full stop.
2. get_test_run_test_cases_v2 (already probed, PASS): PR-NNN/TR-NNN only (no bare integers), pages with p/page_size (max 300, 30 if fetch_steps=true, hard 400 above max), flat {success,info,test_cases}, row keyed by string identifier + configuration_id (no mapping_id concept), flat label fields (latest_status, assignee as flat-ish), self link documented as malformed, large structured filter surface (tags, assignee, status, folder_id, date ranges, free-text query).
3. get_test_cases_for_v1_test_run (this one): accepts TR-NNN OR bare integer (^(TR-)?[0-9]+$) — looser than v2's PR/TR-only route. Pages with p/per_page (max 100, silent fallback to 30 on out-of-range — a soft-failure mode, the opposite of v2's hard 400). Row keyed by integer id + mapping_id (the run-mapping id bulk ops actually take) — richer/heavier row than v2's, with nested objects for status/priority/case_type instead of v2's flat label strings, plus test_case_steps, lcnc_build_map, automation_status, issues, comments_count, metadata, custom_fields. Filter surface is different in kind, not just size: q (generic filter object), shared (return only cross-project-shared cases), source_project_id (slice by contributing project), required[fields] (an allow-list of OPTIONAL columns — a concept neither sibling has), and a sort_by that is trapped by required[fields] (sort column must be included in required[fields] or the call 400s with a named error). Top-level skipped_test_case_ids is unique to this endpoint (cases the review gate excluded) — v2 has no equivalent concept.

VERDICT ON REDUNDANCY: this is NOT a redundant near-duplicate of v2 — it is a genuinely distinct, heavier tool for a different job. v2 is the lightweight, filterable execution-grid view (flat labels, configuration_id, hard-capped paging, big structured filter set) suited to UI-style browsing/searching of a run. This v1 capability is the bulk-ops-oriented view: it is the only one of the three that actually returns mapping_id — the id every bulk mutation on the run (assign, bulk-edit-result, unlink) requires — so any agent workflow that needs to identify or use mapping ids has no substitute; v2 cannot serve that need. The two are complementary, not overlapping: v2 for querying/filtering/browsing a run's cases, this one for enumerating mapping ids to feed into write capabilities, with richer per-case objects (steps, custom_fields, case_type) as a side benefit. No text anywhere in this capability's intent/guidance, nor in what's known of the other two, marks any of the three as legacy/deprecated/preferred over another — there is no 'use instead' or 'replaced by' language. So the real finding is: get_test_run_cases_v1 is the true dead-weight/misleadingly-named one of the trio (a header endpoint masquerading as a case-lister), while v2 and this v1 capability are both live and each earn their place for different callers — a two-way real duplication risk (both list cases, differ in grain/paging/filters) plus one outright misnamed non-lister, not a clean three-way redundant set. Also worth noting per the task's tip: unlike search_test_cases_by_folder_v1's unconditional 200 [], this capability's skipped_test_case_ids:[] here is legitimately empty (no cases were excluded by the review gate for this run) — not a sign of a dead/broken route, since test_cases itself returned real, populated rows.
